newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn falls to new contract lows, and 2-yr low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn falls to new contract lows, and 2-yr low.

text.p: CBOT corn futures fell to new contract lows and fresh two-year lows on near-perfect crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

"The feeling is there is a very high confidence level that the rain that is forecast will occur," said Dan Cekander, grain analyst for FIMAT Futures. "The weather guys have been forecasting rain and that has happened and there are some heavy rains in the forecasts."
The new low for July is $2.45-1/2 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.50 set Thursday. The $2.45-1/2 level is the lowest level for a nearby since April 1995.
The new low for December is $2.35, below the previous low of $2.38-1/4 set Thursday.
Recent warm temperatures and showers have boosted crop production prospects and there have been no outlooks to indicate a shift away from the good crop growing conditions.

Position squaring was noted. USDA Friday released its updated hogs and pigs report, Monday the updated USDA stocks and acreage reports will be released. Also Monday is first notice day for deliveries on the July contract.
Corn closed one to four cents lower, with July down four at $2.46-1/4.

Prudential Securities sold six million bushels of December and Cargill Investor Services sold 2.5 million bushels of December, traders said. ADM Investor Services bought four million bushels of December and Cargill Inc bought four million bushels of July, traders said.

In spread trading, Continental Grain did two million December/July at 11-3/4 cents, premium July, Cargill Inc spread two million July/December at 11-1/2 cents, premium July and Merrill Lynch Futures did 2.5 million December/July at 11-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 91,115 traded Thursday.

In corn options, Term Commodities bought 2,000 December $2.40 calls at 10 cents, Lind Waldock sold 1,000 December $2.30 puts at eight cents and Smith Barney bought 600 September $2.50 calls at 5-3/4 to 5-5/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 24,900 traded Thursday.
